neighbours.label: gardens and land managed as habitat for pollinators and wildlife (attracting bees, butterflies, beneficial insects; pesticides harming them), as against gardening and land use without the wildlife angle
fire: Our neighbours let part of the lawn grow wild to give shelter to wildlife.
Lavender in the border draws bumblebees and other pollinators all summer.
The farmer sowed clover between the rows to feed beneficial insects.
Spraying insecticide on the roses also killed many of the butterflies.
Native asters are a late source of nectar for migrating monarchs.
A small pond in the corner of the yard attracts frogs and dragonflies.
Leaving dead stems over winter gives solitary bees a place to nest.
The council planted hedgerows along the fields as corridors for wildlife.
quiet: Our neighbours let part of the lawn grow long because the mower broke.
Lavender in the border smells lovely and looks good all summer.
The farmer sowed clover between the rows to improve the soil.
Spraying fungicide on the roses stopped the black spot on the leaves.
Native asters are a late source of colour in the front garden.
A small pond in the corner of the yard needs cleaning every spring.
Leaving dead stems over winter makes the garden look untidy.
The council planted hedgerows along the fields to stop soil erosion.
